newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Friday on speculative buying at low levels, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 23,800 yuan ($2,869) per tonne, rising 80 yuan. It opened at 23,700 and hit a low of 23,620.
May closed unchanged at 23,480, June rose 30 to 23,690, July gained 80 to 23,800 and September added 80 to 23,800.
Combined volume fell to 38,980 tonnes from 51,110.
Copper opened lower and continue to fall before speculative buying set in late in the session, pushing the prices up to end at or near their intra-day highs, traders said.
Traders said Friday's rises indicated many investors were optimistic about the short-term market trend.
"Speculative buying was responsible for today's rises, with many investors believing copper futures will rise in the short term," one trader said.
Firm physical prices continued to boost the confidence of long position holders, traders said. Average physical prices were around 23,550 yuan per tonne on Friday in the Shanghai area.
Analysts said they expected copper to rise steadily in the next few days in the absense of fresh market-moving news.
"Improved market sentiment is likely to continue to push copper futures up in the short term," said a second trader.
May fell 50 to 15,500 and June 60 to 15,750.
Combined volume rose to 850 tonnes from 740.
